extraChanges.subject: ExcelLoadOptions transport and ExcelReaderOptions.Transport
extraChanges.note: URI loading takes the same ExcelLoadOptions as local loading. OpenReaderAsync(Uri,ExcelReaderOptions) carries transport policy in its single reader bag.

extraChanges.subject: Excel password association
extraChanges.note: Native output retains a loaded password unless Password is explicitly assigned; clearing encryption updates association only after a successful file commit. Internal native byte encoders remain raw.

extraChanges.subject: Excel load report snapshots
extraChanges.note: Load(path/stream,options,out OfficeConversionReport) freezes native XLS/XLSB import diagnostics rather than retaining a parser/result wrapper. xlsb-unprojected-record carries per-record information in the message.

extraChanges.subject: Excel XML Spreadsheet options
extraChanges.note: The M0 map merges an options type used by both XML import and XML export into ExcelLoadOptions. Import settings belong in ExcelLoadOptions; output-only resource settings must remain with the explicit export operation. This boundary is not yet implemented.

extraChanges.subject: Excel native 3D diagnostics
extraChanges.note: Actual 3D flattening emits chart-flattened; pie-of-pie, stock and surface fallbacks retain their broader approximation codes. Combo findings are emitted per affected series.

extraChanges.subject: Native conversion source settings
extraChanges.note: The front door supplies captured ExcelLoadOptions to the existing native conversion engine, preserving XLS/XLSB codec behavior and fidelity assessment.

extraChanges.subject: Options capture
extraChanges.note: Internal load snapshots copy HTTP allowlists/headers and native decoder/security settings; save snapshots retain explicit password assignment.

extraChanges.subject: Read-only inspection and preservation types use Info
extraChanges.note: Phase A naming follows the approved rule that read-only snapshots end in Info. Geometry properties remain unchanged for Phase B.

extraChanges.change: The canonical workbook data reader opens the current worksheet lazily. SheetNames and metadata-only discovery do not decode cells/shared strings; row/schema access opens one worksheet and normal disposal/cancellation remain active.
extraChanges.reason: The approved GetSheetNames to OpenReader().SheetNames migration must preserve lightweight metadata discovery and its resource-limit behavior.

extraChanges.note: ExcelSaveOptions.Clone() is public so wrappers can set a password on a copy while retaining the distinction between unset and explicitly null passwords. PSWriteOffice uses that copy for native Save.

URI loads snapshot the combined load and transport bag before awaiting HTTP. URI readers clone their complete reader and Transport settings before downloading; admission identity and caller-mutation tests use the canonical single options bag.

ExcelCreateOptions retains template Overwrite and OpenSettings. The separate ExcelTemplateCreateOptions type is internal. Reconstruction fidelity tests retain native table-scope assertions through an artifact fixture helper, while public reconstruction forms are covered by the front-door contracts. Removed one duplicate cancellation assertion that only exercised the deleted SaveAsPdfResultAsync alias.

Specialized static content-safety, provenance and signature inspection entry points are internal native kernels. OfficeDocument.Inspect(path, OfficeInspectOptions) returns OfficeDocumentInfo with selectable typed reports and optional native content. IncludeContent=false preserves inspection without content extraction; original package/signature/provenance guards and explicit provider selection remain in their owning libraries. Provenance takes an independent options snapshot with caller cancellation.

XLSB limits are flattened onto ExcelLoadOptions. The native XlsbImportOptions property is internal; async loads snapshot the complete bag before awaiting, and final cancellation tokens reach native record projection. The original native preservation options model remains for the Phase B visibility pass.

The lazy reader preserves lightweight SheetNames discovery and opens a worksheet on row/schema access. The native XLSX fast path retains its SDK fallback at that deferred boundary. Existing malformed-source and resource-limit tests now exercise schema access rather than expecting row validation from metadata-only construction.

Synchronous OpenReader retains live reader projection settings, including InferSchema and CellValueConverter changes. Async and URI readers still snapshot the full settings before awaiting. Malformed worksheet admission tests consume schema or rows after metadata-only opening instead of expecting eager sheet access.

Password-bearing Load retains encrypted SaveOnDispose without copying plaintext back into the decoder stream. Legacy XLS BOF and truncation classifiers use mapped lowercase diagnostic identifiers. Lazy reader admission tests access schema before asserting malformed styles, shared strings or XML text limits; private XLSB fixture assertions now exercise the public lazy reader boundary. XLSB unprojected record findings use the catalog code and preserve record locations in structured fields.

ExcelDocument.CreateWriter returns ExcelWorkbookWriter. Multiple typed synchronous/asynchronous tables, explicit row callbacks, DataTable and IDataReader reuse the native XLSX row encoder with inline strings and deferred package metadata. OfficeTheme is emitted as native theme/font data. File output uses the existing atomic file commit owner, and failed row sources discard the staging file. Native package, cancellation and non-seekable ownership checks pass on net8.0/net10.0; legacy static entry-point consumer migration remains part of Phase B.

The existing OfficeChartSeries model becomes root OfficeIMO.OfficeSeries, adding numeric typed-selector factories. OfficeChartKind merges into the M1 OfficeChartType enum. Native chart writers and all in-repo type consumers use that single enum/model; typed and nameof-based AddChart overloads reuse the existing shared native chart data pipeline. Core builds on all three macOS targets with zero warnings; six typed native chart artifact cases and 166 shared chart regression cases pass on each modern framework.

The shared declared-schema projection handles public properties, fields and string-keyed dictionaries without arbitrary object graph reflection. Word also retains rectangular text/matrix input and an explicit dynamic-object overload; PowerPoint retains configurable object flattening with an explicit configure argument; Excel retains DataTable values and returns native ExcelTable wrappers. Focused authoring tests: 10/10 per modern target; final table signature check: 4/4 per target.

Typed and DataTable AddTable honor shared projection and alignment options alongside ExcelTableOptions.Projection; table-local selection/order and formatting take precedence over their advanced counterparts. Native DataTable row and selected-column bounds are checked before formatting or copying values.

ExcelColumnWidth is a dependency-free value type in OfficeIMO.Excel with Characters/Length factories, explicit worksheet-aware conversions and unit-preserving equality. The existing default-font column geometry resolver remains the only font measurement path. Native legacy projections/writers, adapters, reports, examples, tests and mechanical PowerShell setters preserve their previous numeric units. Inspection ExcelColumnInfo.Width and ExcelRowInfo.Height use nullable ExcelColumnWidth; codecs retain internal numeric values in the native units.

extraChanges.note: ExcelColumnWidth.CharacterCount and PhysicalLength expose nullable, unit-preserving inspection without requiring a live worksheet or font resolver. Internal StoredWidth and StoredHeight retain exact native values for codecs and adapters. Reader, Google Sheets, HTML, PDF, OpenDocument, iWork, markup and PowerShell summary consumers perform explicit conversions to preserve their existing output units. Native and legacy inspection round trips keep character widths and point heights.

ExcelWorkbookWriter.WriteTable returns ExcelDataSetImportResult, or Task<ExcelDataSetImportResult> for asynchronous sources, with final observed row/column counts, sanitized sheet/table names and occupied range. The existing tabular result model is shared by imports and streaming writes. Results retain only schema and counts, never source rows. IDataReader headers use the existing native blank-name and duplicate-name normalization.

PSWriteOffice and the CLI direct XLSX reader exports and the combined AOT smoke use CreateWriter(...).WriteTable(...). PowerShell preserves ReaderData as its default table name, Sheet1 for blank worksheet names, native header normalization, caller resource ownership and the existing atomic file commit. Remaining static row/reader/DataSet consumers and the superseded public entry points remain pending the writer-removal batch.
PowerShell encrypted workbook lifecycle and HTML conversion tests exercise the current API directly; removed LoadEncrypted probes no longer bypass these workflows.

Mechanical PowerShell save calls assign Password=null explicitly for unencrypted output. This preserves plain-copy and subsequent-save behavior after loading an encrypted document; omitted native save passwords continue to inherit source encryption as documented. Excel save-option snapshots retain preflight and formula settings. Existing encrypted-source overwrite guards still require an explicit -Password.
Encrypted-package routing errors point to Load with ExcelLoadOptions.Password and OpenReader with ExcelReaderOptions.Password, replacing guidance for the removed encrypted factories.

ExcelMacroProject and ExcelPageBreak are attached authoring models. Removed or replaced handles cannot operate on a replacement at the same package URI or worksheet index. Ignored-error results use the existing immutable region metadata, and TOC backlinks return the existing hyperlink metadata keyed by worksheet. Format-specific Add methods return their created model or metadata. Macro-handle checks and operations use the workbook lock together, so concurrent replacement cannot redirect an old handle.
